meanings.note: Male sibling. Common masculine noun meaning 'brother, cousin' in everyday Russian.
in двоюродный/троюродный брат, often shortened to брат

examples.text: Мой старший брат живёт в Москве.
examples.trans: My older brother lives in Moscow.

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

'брать взятку' = to take a bribe. Prefix 'вз-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'ятка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'bribe' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: За взятку. За очень большую взятку.
examples.trans: For a bribe. For a very large bribe.

meanings.note: 'взять на работу' = to give someone a job
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зместить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to compensate'.

examples.trans: We want to compensate your damage.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и возместить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to compensate on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'змутительно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Это просто возмутительно, так нельзя работать!
examples.trans: This is simply outrageous, you cannot work like this!

examples.text: Гость ведёт себя совершенно возмутительно в зале.
examples.trans: The guest is behaving completely outrageously in the dining room.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: жить в гостинице = to stay at a hotel

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'make, cause'.

examples.text: Что, я зря пришла? Я надела костюм зайки!
examples.trans: What, did I come for nothing? I put on a bunny costume!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: Governs на + accusative. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'мекать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hint, imply'.

examples.text: На кого ты сейчас намекаешь, майор?
examples.trans: Who are you hinting at right now, Major?

examples.text: А я ни на кого не намекаю.
examples.trans: And I am not hinting at anyone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write', paired with 'писать'.

examples.text: А зачем? Я сам сделал так, чтобы он его написал.
examples.trans: And why would I? I'm the one who made him write it.

Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
